title: Screen 1: Tide (weekly trend)
description: evaluate_tide() in app/signals/triple_screen.py: BULLISH / BEARISH / NEUTRAL from weekly MACD-Histogram slope plus 13/26-week EMA relationship.

checklist.step: Implement slope detection on weekly MACD-Histogram (rising/falling/flat)
Combine with 13-week vs 26-week EMA relationship per docs/Analyse.md §2
Return NEUTRAL (not a forced guess) when the two signals disagree or data is ambiguous
Write unit tests covering all three outputs (BULLISH/BEARISH/NEUTRAL) with fixed weekly OHLCV fixtures
Run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing and confirm no regression

decisions.decision: evaluate_tide() classifies the weekly MACD-Histogram slope from only the last two histogram points (macd_histogram(weekly_close).iloc[-1] vs .iloc[-2]), and calls it 'flat' when the step between them, expressed as a fraction of the latest weekly close (|step| / |latest_close|), is below 0.001 (0.1%). BULLISH requires slope=='rising' AND ema(13) > ema(26); BEARISH requires slope=='falling' AND ema(13) < ema(26); every other combination (flat slope, slope/EMA disagreement, or fewer than 2 weekly bars to even compute a slope) returns NEUTRAL.
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md §2 pins the two inputs (weekly MACD-Histogram slope, 13/26-week EMA relationship) and says tide is NEUTRAL 'if MACD-H slope is flat/ambiguous', but deliberately does not define the flat threshold -- indicator-macd-histogram's own decisions entry explicitly deferred that choice to this task rather than baking a threshold into the indicator module. Chose a two-point (last step) slope over a longer lookback (e.g. comparing the latest point to a 3- or 5-week-back average) because it matches the doc's literal 'rising/falling' language most directly, is trivial to hand-verify in tests, and avoids inventing a second undocumented window-length parameter on top of the undocumented threshold. Chose to normalize the flat threshold by the latest close price (a relative/percentage cutoff) rather than a fixed absolute dollar threshold, because MACD-Histogram magnitude scales with the underlying price -- a fixed absolute cutoff (e.g. 0.01) would misclassify a $5 stock's genuine moves as never-flat and a $500 stock's noise as always-flat; 0.1% of price is a small-but-nonzero cutoff chosen to filter near-zero noise while still classifying any histogram step that's a meaningful fraction of the price as directional. Rejected requiring a longer minimum history (e.g. >=26 weeks) before evaluating tide at all: ema() already handles short series correctly via its documented first-value seed (see indicator-ema's decisions entry), docs/Analyse.md §8's '~200 trading days' guidance is a data-acquisition recommendation for the app as a whole, not a hard gate this specific function needs to enforce; the only hard guard added is len(weekly_ohlcv) < 2 (can't compute a slope with fewer than 2 points at all), which returns NEUTRAL as 'ambiguous data' per checklist item 3, not a fabricated BULLISH/BEARISH guess.

decisions.decision: Fixed the duplicate-EMA(26) finding by adding `macd_components()`/`MacdComponents` to app/indicators/macd.py, exposing ema_fast, ema_slow, macd_line, signal_line and histogram from one computation; `macd_histogram()` is now a thin wrapper returning just `.histogram`, so its existing callers/tests are unaffected. evaluate_tide() now calls `macd_components(weekly_close)` once and reuses `.ema_slow` as EMA(26), calling `ema(weekly_close, 13)` separately only for EMA(13) -- EMA(26) is no longer computed twice per evaluate_tide() call.
decisions.rationale: Rejected inlining the MACD line/signal-line math directly into triple_screen.py to avoid touching macd.py at all: that would duplicate the MACD construction that docs/Analyse.md §4 says lives in one place, and would drift from app.indicators.macd's own (already-tested) implementation over time. Rejected memoizing ema() calls (e.g. functools.lru_cache) instead of restructuring macd.py: it doesn't fix the actual layering problem (macd_histogram would still internally recompute EMA(26) even if the outer ema() calls were cached) and adds cache-invalidation complexity for a data size (weekly bars) where the duplicate computation was already cheap. Chose a structured dataclass result (MacdComponents) over returning a tuple/dict of series, for attribute-access readability and because other planned consumers (e.g. impulse-system, which also needs MACD-Histogram direction) can reuse whichever intermediate they need without guessing tuple order.

decisions.decision: evaluate_tide() now returns a frozen dataclass `TideResult(trend, weekly_macd_histogram_slope)` instead of a bare trend string, mirroring TideScreen's (app/api/schemas.py) two required fields field-for-field. The previously-private `_macd_histogram_slope` helper was promoted to a public `macd_histogram_slope(histogram, latest_close)` function, now taking an already-computed histogram Series (and the latest close) instead of a raw close-price Series, so it composes with the new `macd_components()` without recomputing the histogram a second time.
decisions.rationale: Directly fixes the finding: a future API-wiring task can populate both TideScreen fields from one evaluate_tide() call, instead of either importing an underscore-prefixed helper across the module boundary or reimplementing slope classification independently (which risked drift if the threshold/algorithm changed later). Considered returning a plain (trend, slope) tuple instead of a named dataclass -- rejected for readability: positional tuple unpacking is easy to get backwards at a call site, whereas `.trend`/`.weekly_macd_histogram_slope` attribute access is self-documenting and matches the schema names exactly. Considered a dict keyed by the schema field names -- rejected as strictly worse than a dataclass (no attribute access, no static typing benefit, same string-key fragility). Considered leaving evaluate_tide() returning a bare string and only adding the new public macd_histogram_slope() as a separately-callable function -- rejected because a future caller would still have to re-invoke it (and recompute the histogram/threshold) independently to get the slope for the *same* evaluation, reintroducing exactly the drift risk the finding flagged; bundling both outputs into one return guarantees they're computed together and always stay consistent. Updated this task's own tests (test_triple_screen.py) and macd.py's tests (test_macd.py, covering the new macd_components()) to match; nothing outside this module referenced evaluate_tide()'s return value yet, so no other call sites needed updating.

decisions.decision: No change to evaluate_tide()'s categorical (BULLISH/BEARISH/NEUTRAL) output is needed to support docs/Analyse.md §6's 'mixed' (50%) tide-alignment confidence scoring -- but correcting the premise this finding was handed down with: `app/signals/confidence.py` has no `score_tide_alignment()` function today (grepped the whole backend/ tree -- no such symbol exists anywhere); `compute_confidence()`/`confidence_band()` are still `NotImplementedError` stubs, and the `confidence-scoring` task itself is still `state: "planned"` (not started, not even `implementing`). So the 'confidence-scoring.json's score_tide_alignment() already handles this pragmatically' framing wasn't literally verifiable against existing code, and this task's own instructions say to treat that as a real gap rather than just recording a no-op decision. What *does* resolve it: the previous decisions entry above (exposing `weekly_macd_histogram_slope` alongside `trend` in `TideResult`) already gives a future `score_tide_alignment()` everything it needs to distinguish the two ways a NEUTRAL trend arises -- slope=='flat' (genuinely ambiguous, docs/Analyse.md §2's literal NEUTRAL trigger) vs. slope in ('rising','falling') but overridden to NEUTRAL by a disagreeing 13/26-week EMA relationship (the 'mixed' case §6 implies) -- purely from TideResult's two existing fields, with no need for evaluate_tide() to expose a fourth categorical trend value or raw EMA numbers. Added an end-to-end test (test_neutral_slope_rising_but_ema_disagrees) that reaches this exact 'mixed' state with real, unmocked indicator math (a sharp 2-week rally after a 30-week decline) and confirms `weekly_macd_histogram_slope=='rising'` while `trend=='NEUTRAL'`, proving the information is actually there to be consumed, not just asserted in a comment.
decisions.rationale: Considered adding a fourth trend value (e.g. 'BULLISH_MIXED'/'BEARISH_MIXED') directly in evaluate_tide() to satisfy §6 literally -- rejected: this task's own checklist item 3 and its first decisions entry above already require NEUTRAL 'when the two signals disagree' (a requirement the original pr-reviewer pass explicitly verified against docs/Analyse.md §2 and did not flag as wrong), docs/Analyse.md §5's Signal Logic table only ever gates BUY/SELL on Tide==BULLISH/BEARISH with no 'mixed' tide value mentioned there at all, and inventing a 4th/5th enum value now -- before the confidence-scoring task that would actually consume it has even started, let alone designed its own data needs -- risks guessing wrong about a shape nobody has designed against yet and would need touching TideScreen's schema (`trend: Trend`) too. Left the §5/§6 doc-level tension itself (pre-existing, not introduced by this PR, per the original pr-reviewer pass) for the confidence-scoring task to resolve when it actually implements score_tide_alignment(), since that's the task whose checklist and scope literally cover this scoring logic.

comments.summary: Non-blocking (reuse/efficiency): evaluate_tide() computes ema(weekly_close, 26) itself even though macd_histogram (called one line earlier via _macd_histogram_slope) already computes EMA(close, 26) internally as its default 'slow' EMA -- same series, same period, computed twice per call. Cheap at current data sizes (weekly bars); eliminating it would need macd.py's API to expose its intermediate EMAs, a real tradeoff against it staying a pure 'return the histogram' function. Worth a look only if macd.py is touched again for other reasons.

Non-blocking (forward-compatibility): evaluate_tide() returns only the BULLISH/BEARISH/NEUTRAL trend string, discarding the rising/falling/flat slope classification, but TideScreen in schemas.py already declares both `trend` and `weekly_macd_histogram_slope` as required response fields, and the helper that computes the slope (_macd_histogram_slope) is private. Whichever task wires up the /analysis endpoint will need to either import the underscore-prefixed helper across module boundaries or recompute the slope independently (risking drift if the threshold/algorithm changes later). Nothing broken today -- evaluate_tide()'s return type matches this task's own description/checklist exactly -- but flagging now so the API-wiring task doesn't have to rediscover it.

Observation, not a bug: docs/Analyse.md §2 only names a flat/ambiguous slope as the NEUTRAL trigger, while §6's confidence-weighting table implies a 'mixed' (slope/EMA disagree) case that's still categorically bullish/bearish with reduced confidence. This implementation makes any slope/EMA disagreement NEUTRAL, per the task's own checklist item 3, which forecloses that 'mixed' scenario. Pre-existing tension in the source doc, not introduced by this PR -- flagging for whoever builds the confidence-score task so they don't discover it's unreachable code.
